paper_metadata.title: The B2 phase-driven microstructural heterogeneities and twinning enable ultrahigh cryogenic strength and large ductility in NiCoCr-based medium-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: we designed heterogeneous (NiCoCr) 88 Al 10 Ta 2 (at.%) duplex medium-entropy alloy (MEA) comprising the face-centered-cubic (FCC) matrix and the B2 phase
A comparison of the (c1) σy vs . εT , (c2) σUTS vs . εT and (c3) σUTS vs. σy of the present Al10Ta2 MEA at 298 K with reported FCC-based M/HEAs reinforced by various secondary phases
An ultra-strong-yet-ductile heterogeneous structured Al10Ta2 MEA was fabricated via elaborate microstructural design.

The Al10Ta2 MEA was prepared by arc-melting technique under a pure Ar atmosphere. The purity for each element is above 99.95%, and the ingots were re-melted five times with electromagnetic stirring to avoid chemical non-homogeneity. Then the ingots with a dimension of 80 × 25 × 15 mm 3 were subjected to the homogenization treatment (HT) at 1225 ◦C for 24 h followed by WQ.

Subsequently, these HT samples were directly hot-rolled (HR) at 1150 ◦C to sheets by multi-pass with a thickness reduction of ∼70% followed by WQ to retain a suitable density of dislocations in the fully recrystallized matrix, particularly, making the blocky B2 phase turn to lath-shaped one.
